intro.title: Discover Tsar Simeon Garden Park
intro.description: Welcome to "Tsar Simeon Garden" Park, widely recognized as the central Tsar Simeon Garden in Plovdiv. Located in the heart of Plovdiv, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria, this destination serves as a primary hub for travelers visiting the region. Created in the late 19th century, it offers a unique combination of natural beauty, historic architecture, and cultural heritage. When visiting, you can easily explore surrounding historical landmarks, including the Ancient Roman Stadium and the Plovdiv Old Town.

visitGuide.title: Visit Tips
items: Best time to visit is spring when flowers are blooming.
The park is ideal for walks and picnics.
Don't miss the Water Tower and historic statues.

sections.title: History & Creation
sections.content: Tsar Simeon Garden Park was created in 1892 according to the design of the Swiss landscape architect Lucien Chevalas. The park is named after Tsar Simeon I, who ruled Bulgaria in the 9th and 10th centuries.

sections.title: Architecture & Design
sections.content: The park was designed in the typical style of its time with wide alleys, decorative ponds, and diverse vegetation. The historic Water Tower beside the park is a landmark of Plovdiv's water-supply history.

sections.title: Location & Nature
sections.content: Located in the center of Plovdiv, the park covers an area of about 18 hectares. It offers cool shade in summer and is a favorite place for walks for both locals and tourists.

sections.title: Preservation & Management
sections.content: The park is maintained by Plovdiv Municipality and is a protected area. Over the years, numerous restorations have been carried out to preserve its historical appearance.

seasonal.title: Seasonal Visiting Strategy
seasonal.subtitle: Based on Plovdiv's long-term continental climate (warm summers, cold winters), here is how each season shapes a visit.

rows.climate: Mild and green; flowers in full bloom, with the occasional shower.
rows.bestTime: Mid-morning to late afternoon; comfortable on most days.
rows.bring: Light jacket, comfortable shoes, small umbrella.
rows.notes: The flower alleys and the early Singing Fountains season are the highlights.

rows.climate: Hot and dry; daytime peaks often above 30°C.
rows.bestTime: Early morning and evening; fountain shows after sunset.
rows.bring: Sun hat, sunscreen, water bottle, light clothing.
rows.notes: The Singing Fountains run in summer – cooler evenings are the best window.

rows.climate: Warm, golden and calm; fewer crowds than summer.
rows.bestTime: Daytime walks; fountain shows move to earlier hours.
rows.notes: Stable, pleasant weather makes this a favourite season for photos.

rows.climate: Cold, sometimes below freezing; possible snow and fog.
rows.bestTime: Midday, when it is brightest and warmest.
rows.bring: Warm coat, hat, gloves, non-slip shoes.
rows.notes: A quiet atmosphere and architectural views in deep greens and white.

itineraries.title: Itineraries & Routes
itineraries.subtitle: Suggested ways to explore the park by time and by travel style. Adjust them to your own pace.

halfDay.title: Half-day highlights
halfDay.desc: Enter from the Central Square, stroll the main alleys to the historic Water Tower, pause at the fountains and flower beds, then return via the shaded promenade. About 1.5–2 hours at a relaxed pace.

fullDay.title: Full-day deep visit
fullDay.desc: Pair the morning walk with surrounding landmarks – the Ancient Roman Stadium and Plovdiv Old Town. Add a café stop and the Singing Fountains in the evening for a complete day.

items.title: Families with children
items.desc: Use the flat main alleys and the children's playground; pack water and snacks, and keep the walk short and playful.

items.title: Photographers & nature
items.desc: Golden hour near the fountains and Water Tower, spring blossoms and autumn colours; bring a light tripod for the evening shows.

items.title: Low-effort / accessible
items.desc: Stay on the step-free central paths, use nearby benches for rests, and plan around shade and the warmest part of the day.

items.question: Where is "Tsar Simeon Garden" Park located?
items.answer: "Tsar Simeon Garden" Park is located in Plovdiv, Plovdiv Province, Bulgaria.

items.question: Is Tsar Simeon Garden free to visit?
items.answer: Yes, "Tsar Simeon Garden" Park is a public space and is free to visit year-round.

items.question: What are the opening hours of the park?
items.answer: The park is open to visitors year-round, 24 hours a day. There is no entrance fee.

items.question: Is there an entrance fee?
items.answer: No, entrance to Tsar Simeon Garden Park is free for all visitors.

items.question: Are there guided tours available?
items.answer: The park can be explored independently. Information signs in several languages are placed at key locations.

items.question: Is the park accessible for wheelchair users?
items.answer: Yes, the main alleys are flat and accessible for wheelchairs. There are also special paths for people with reduced mobility.

items.question: How much time should I plan for a visit?
items.answer: Usually 1-2 hours are enough for a walk through the park, but you can stay longer to enjoy the surroundings.

items.question: Is the park suitable for families with children?
items.answer: Yes, the park is ideal for families with children – it has wide alleys, green lawns, and children's playgrounds.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: The park is adjacent to the Central Square and the main pedestrian street (Knyaz Alexander I). It's only a 10-15 minute walk from the Roman Stadium and the Old Town.
transport.fromStationDesc: From Plovdiv Central Railway Station or Bus Station South, it's a 15-20 minute walk or a short bus ride (lines 7, 20, 26) to the center.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Plovdiv is easily accessible from Sofia by bus or train (approx. 2 hours). Plovdiv Airport is about 15 km away and can be reached by taxi.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Many bus lines (e.g., 1, 11, 20) stop near the Central Post Office or Trimontium Hotel, just a few minutes' walk from the park entrances.
transport.walkingDesc: The park is seamlessly connected to other historical sites in the center. Walking is highly recommended as part of a city tour.
transport.drivingDesc: Navigate to ul. „Veliko Tarnovo“ 11A. Note that the city center is mostly a paid parking zone (Blue Zone). Use public parking near the Central Square or Trimontium Hotel.
transport.taxiDesc: Taxis and app-based rides are easy to find at the railway and bus stations and at the airport. Ask the driver to use the meter or agree on a fare first; a ride from the center to the park is usually short and inexpensive.

bestTime.title: Best Time to Visit
bestTime.subtitle: The garden is beautiful in every season, but a summer evening with the Singing Fountains is an experience not to be missed:

seasons.title: Spring (March–May)
seasons.text: The flower alleys are in full bloom and temperatures are pleasant. The best time for photos and leisurely walks with fewer visitors.

seasons.title: Summer (June–August)
seasons.text: Singing Fountains season! Choose the late afternoon and early evening – it is cooler, and the musical light-and-water shows are in full swing.

seasons.title: Autumn (September–October)
seasons.text: Golden colours and soft light make walks especially pleasant. The fountain programme usually continues, with show times moving earlier.

seasons.title: Winter (November–February)
seasons.text: The quiet winter park offers tranquillity and unique shots of the architecture in deep greens and white.

bestTime.note: The Singing Fountains typically run from June to the end of September, Thursday to Saturday, free of charge. In summer the show starts around 9:00–9:30 PM, and in autumn around 8:30 PM. The exact schedule is announced annually by Plovdiv Municipality.

items.desc: Within walking distance in the city center there are hotels, guest houses, apartments, and other types of lodging across different categories.

items.desc: The city center offers shopping malls, supermarkets, and souvenir shops – convenient for buying food and water before a walk.

items.desc: Fuel stations can be found around the center, while electric vehicle chargers are located at public parking lots and shopping facilities.

items.title: Families & Children
items.desc: The park has a children's playground, rest benches, and large green lawns – ideal for family strolls and picnics.

history.title: Historical Timeline
history.subtitle: Key moments in the history of Tsar Simeon Garden:

items.title: Created for the First Exhibition
items.text: The garden was created in 1892 for the First Bulgarian Agricultural-Industrial Exhibition, designed by Swiss landscape architect Lucien Chevalas. The exhibition's successor is today's International Fair – Plovdiv.

items.title: Named after Tsar Simeon
items.text: After the exhibition closed, the garden was named "Tsar Simeon's" in honor of Tsar Simeon I (893–927), whose reign is considered the "Golden Age" of medieval Bulgaria.

items.title: Growth & Monuments
items.text: Over the decades the garden became the city's main park – monuments, sculptures, and fountains were added, including the Demeter fountain by Italian sculptor Arnoldo Zòcchi, as well as the Fisherman and Bear fountains.

items.title: A Monument of Park Art
items.text: Tsar Simeon Garden was declared a monument of park art and is protected under Bulgarian cultural heritage law.

items.title: The Singing Fountains
items.text: In the garden's pond, the "Singing Fountains" put on musical light-and-water shows in summer – an emblematic experience for residents and visitors alike.

legends.title: Stories & Legends
legends.subtitle: Historical facts and curious stories about the garden:

items.title: The "Minister of Flowers"
items.text: Swiss architect Lucien Chevalas became known for his floral compositions and was called the "minister of flowers" by his contemporaries. The garden he created was among Plovdiv's finest public spaces from the very start.

items.title: The Demeter Fountain
items.text: Created by Italian sculptor Arnoldo Zòcchi, the fountain is the only surviving original object from the First Bulgarian Exhibition of 1892 and has kept its memory alive for decades.

items.title: Summer Nights with the Singing Fountains
items.text: During the warm months the fountain pond comes alive with music, lights, and water jets. For generations of Plovdiv residents, the "Singing Fountains" are part of the city's summer memories.

items.title: The Name of the Garden
items.text: The garden bears the name of Tsar Simeon I – the ruler under whom medieval Bulgaria reached its cultural and political peak. Set in the heart of the city, it serves today as its "green living room".

etiquette.title: Visit Guidelines & Tips
items: Stick to the walkways and avoid stepping on flower beds and lawns.
Keep noise down and respect other visitors and open-air concerts.
Do not feed or disturb the animals in the park (birds and others).
Dispose of waste in the recycling bins.
Do not enter the ponds – some are decorative.
Supervise children while playing on the playground.
